content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new here and just getting started with [company_name] [product_name]. I purchased the controller about three weeks ago and have been having trouble setting up Dynamic DNS for remote access. I'd like to be able to download a program to the controller over the internet. When connecting via Dynamic DNS, I see a green bar, which seems positive, but as soon as I try any action—like downloading a program—the configuration software asks for a remote access password I never set. An 'http authentication failed' error appears (see attachment). I've tried various password combinations, installed the software on another computer, and used different routers, but nothing helps. My webserver access works perfectly from anywhere, so the issue seems confined to the configuration software. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated. Thank you!
My controller type: [article_no] Configuration software version: [version_no]

Is your [product_name] device the only one connected to the network? Remember to enable remote access in Access Control. In the configuration software, enter your DynDNS address when connecting—leave out the 'HTTP://' prefix, but add ': 8080' at the end.

Thanks for the quick response. Yes, I have only one controller on my network. I've already enabled remote access in Access Control. I always try the address without 'http://'—if I include it, the green bar doesn't appear.
Did you click 'Apply' after making changes in the remote access and password settings? Are you entering the address with spaces before and after ':8080'?

Yes to both questions. I've reset the remote password and checked the access box multiple times. The software asks to put the controller in RUN mode, and I've tried every possible combination, including longer passwords and leaving it blank. When I format the address as you've described (IP space : space Port), it seems okay at the connection screen, but once I try any action, it requests a password again.
Did you enter a numeric IP address for the connection, or did you use your DynDNS address? Have you tried using the password set up for remote control in Access Control?

Yes, it's my static IP address. With IP:8080, I can access the webserver from any browser and check status from anywhere. I also tried a NO IP Dynamic DNS service—it just converts the numeric IP to a domain name, but the password problem remained. I've tried the password from remote access, the webserver password, and every possible version of '[product_name]', but nothing works. It's confusing that the webserver access is fine, but the configuration software consistently fails authentication.
Try using port 80 instead of 8080—it might solve the problem.

Perhaps these steps could help: 1. How do you enable and access the webserver on [product_name] [version_no]? 2. Router settings: Port forwarding—external port 8080 mapped to internal port 8080 for the controller's IP address. 3. From your office PC, use either 'http://[public IP]:8080' or 'http://[domain]:8080'.

I've followed the manual closely and everything matches your description. The webserver is fully functional, so I would expect the configuration software to work too. The mobile app connects without a problem, even from abroad. I have a legal copy of the software on CD, and have tested on other PCs, but still can't connect.
Are you from Germany? I set up my DynDNS using FRITZ!Box service. If you're from Germany, please send me a private message so we can discuss further.

I'm from Poland. My router is a 'TP LINK'. If anyone has ideas or suggestions on what to check next, please let me know. Summary: 1. I can connect via Ethernet to my controller. 2. Webserver access works from anywhere; port forwarding seems correct. 3. The mobile app runs and connects with no issues, even from outside the country. 4. DNS in the configuration software fails—green bar appears but then asks for a password. 5. Access Control settings and passwords have been verified; no password combination works. The basic controller setup is proving quite challenging.
Can you provide the exact model of your TP-Link router?
It's a TP-Link TL-WR841N, version 13, 300Mbps Wireless N Router.
I recommend trying port 102 or 103. With my previous setup on [product_name], those ports worked fine.
Hello, I was finally able to connect via DNS and can offer assistance if needed.

On a TP-Link router, make sure to activate the DMZ function in the firewall and assign the controller's IP address. I did this until my TP-Link failed; the replacement router didn't have the same issue.
This discussion is about seven years old and the solution wasn't shared. How did you resolve the issue? I'm experiencing the same problem.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have difficulty with remote authentication when connecting to [product_name] [version_no] devices through the configuration software using Dynamic DNS. While webserver access is reliable via browser, the configuration software persistently requests a password, causing 'http authentication failed' errors. Changing passwords, ports, and access settings does not resolve the problem, suggesting an interface or design limitation for remote programming over Dynamic DNS.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable, straightforward remote access and programming of [product_name] [version_no] using Dynamic DNS in the configuration software, with authentication processes that function as seamlessly as the browser-based webserver connection.
